prs.title: fix(v4): stop the memoizer copying every issue below each recursive node (#6705)
prs.taskSummary:
fix(v4): stop the memoizer copying every issue below each recursive node (#6705)

The memoizer cached each container's result with a full copy of its
issues, paths included, so a recursive schema stored every issue below
each node again at every level: memory grew with the cube of the depth.
A 15 KB reply chain with 2000 failing leaves at the bottom of an
800-deep `next` chain held ~5 GB and crashed Node at its default heap.

An entry now keeps each issue by reference beside its path length, and
a cache hit hands out a copy with the path cut back to that length.
Receivers only ever prepend to

prs.title: fix(v4): keep a memoized node's cached issues private to the cache (#6443)
prs.taskSummary:
fix(v4): keep a memoized node's cached issues private to the cache (#6443)

An issue belongs to the payload it was raised into, and every receiver prefixes
a path onto it in place. The memoizer handed the same issue objects to every
visitor of a shared node, so the second visitor prefixed onto the first one's
path: a DAG-shaped input reaching one invalid node twice reported
["right","left","name"] twice instead of ["left","name"] and ["right","name"].

Only the jitless object path is affected today, because the object JIT copies
each issue before prefixing it and util.prefixIssues does not.

prs.title: fix(v4): check array, set and map size bounds before parsing elements (#6652)

fix(v4): check array, set and map size bounds before parsing elements (#6652)

.max(), .length() and .size() ran after every element was walked, so an
oversized input built one issue per bad element before the bound was
reported. Leading size checks now reject the input first, both in the
interpreter and in the compiled path.

Fixes #6643

prs.title: fix(v4): align record keys and intersection strictness with TypeScript (#6412)
prs.taskSummary:
fix(v4): align record keys and intersection strictness with TypeScript (#6412)

* fix(record): classify an out-of-set key by whether the key schema is enumerable

An enumerable key schema (z.enum, z.literal([...])) declares which keys the
record owns, so a key outside that set is unrecognized. A non-enumerable one
(regex, refine) is a constraint every key must satisfy, so a failing key is
invalid. Only the first is reconcilable against the other side of an
intersection, which handleIntersectionResults already does for
unrecognized_keys.

The branch that emitted the issue keyed off def.partial

diff.text: function handleIntersectionResults(result: ParsePayload, left: ParsePayload, right: ParsePayload): ParsePayload {
// Track which side(s) report each key as unrecognized
// Track which side(s) reject each key. A key rejection is reported only when
// BOTH sides reject it, so a key owned by one branch survives the other's
// key schema. strictObject reports these as unrecognized_keys; a record with
// an open key schema reports one invalid_key per key.
const unrecKeys = new Map<string, { l?: true; r?: true }>();

reasons.detail: Aborted check was moved to after mergeValues so intersection merging now runs even when one side aborted (invalid input), and only returns early if merge also fails; this can throw 'Unmergable intersection' or return a merged value instead of correctly aborting, and the new aggregated filtering can drop unrecognized_keys reporting when both sides reject via different codes.

reasons.detail: Moves util.aborted(result) check from before mergeValues to only inside !merged.valid, so an aborted intersection that is still mergeable will no longer abort and will return a merged value instead of the error.

container instance; zod/mini injects nothing and links none of this.
Core's whole share is one interface, one `_zod` field, one changed
allocation line per container, and one line in runChecks -- the memoizer
is read once at construction, so a schema without one runs exactly the
code it runs today

들여쓰기된 코드 안에서 여러 줄 문자열을 작성하고 싶을 때, `dedent`를 태그드 템플릿 리터럴로 사용하세요. 비어 있지 않은 줄들이 공통으로 가진 가장 작은 들여쓰기를 찾아서 모든 줄에서 제거하기 때문에, 줄 사이의 상대적인 들여쓰기 차이는 유지돼요. 첫 줄이나 마지막 줄이 공백만 포함하면 제거돼요.
// 삽입된 값은 들여쓰기를 제거하기 전에 채워져요

diff.text: Removes the common leading whitespace from every line of a multi-line string.
Use it to write multi-line strings that follow your code's indentation, without the indentation ending up in the actual string.

Use `dedent` as a tagged template literal to write multi-line strings inside indented code. It finds the smallest indentation shared by the non-empty lines and removes it from every line, so relative indentation differences between lines are preserved. If the first or last line contains only whitespace, it is removed.
// The indentation from the code is removed
// Relative indentation between lines is preserved
// Interpolated values are inserted before the indentation is removed
Lines that contain only whitespace become empty lines, and Windows line endings (`\r\n`) are normalized to `\n`.
- `values` (`unknown[]`): The values to interpolate into the template literal.
(`string`): The string with the common leading whitespace removed.
Use `dedent` as a regular function when you want to remove the common leading whitespace from a string already stored in a variable.
// Remove the common indentation from an existing string
(`string`): The string with the common leading whitespace removed.

To combine `dedent` with another tag function, pass the tag function as an argument, like `dedent(tagFn)`. The new tag function receives template strings with the common leading whitespace already removed.
// A tag function that runs the Python code it receives
// Wrapping it with dedent makes it receive dedented code
- `tagFn` (`(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) => T`): The tag function to compose.
(`(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) => T`): A new tag function that removes the common leading whitespace from the template strings before passing them to `tagFn`.

diff.text: 从多行字符串的每一行中移除共同的前导缩进。
即使按照代码的缩进书写多行字符串，缩进也不会出现在实际的字符串中。
当您想在有缩进的代码中书写多行字符串时，请将 `dedent` 用作标签模板字面量。它会找出非空行共同拥有的最小缩进，并从每一行中移除，因此行与行之间的相对缩进差异会被保留。如果第一行或最后一行只包含空白，则会被移除。
// 代码中的缩进会被移除
// 行与行之间的相对缩进会被保留
// 插值会在移除缩进之前插入
只包含空白的行会变成空行，Windows 换行符（`\r\n`）会被规范化为 `\n`。
// 只包含空白的行会变成空行
- `str` (`TemplateStringsArray`): 要移除缩进的模板字面量。
- `values` (`unknown[]`): 要插入到模板字面量中的值。
(`string`): 移除了共同前导缩进的字符串。
如果您想从已经保存在变量中的字符串中移除共同的缩进，请将 `dedent` 用作普通函数。
// 从已有的字符串中移除共同的缩进
(`string`): 移除了共同前导缩进的字符串。
如果您想与其他标签函数组合使用，请像 `dedent(tagFn)` 一样将标签函数作为参数传入。这样创建的新标签函数会接收到已经移除共同缩进的模板字符串。
// 执行接收到的 Python 代码的标签函数
// 用 dedent 包装后，它会接收到移除缩进后的代码
- `tagFn` (`(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) => T`): 要组合的标签函数。
(`(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]) => T`): 返回一个新的标签函数，它会先移除模板字符串中共同的前导缩进，再将其传给 `tagFn`。

Sessions have two independent expiration controls, and you can use either or both:
- `maxAge` is an **absolute** lifetime, counted from when the session was created. It is reached however active the user is.
- `idleTimeout` is a **sliding** lifetime, counted from the last request. An active user stays signed in; an idle one is signed out.
idleTimeout: 60 * 30, // signed out after 30 minutes of inactivity...

With `idleTimeout` set, H3 moves the idle window forward by resealing the session cookie with the reseal time stamped into it. `createdAt` is left untouched, which is what lets `maxAge` still act as a hard cap on top. The cookie `Expires` is set to whichever limit runs out first.

If you are coming from `express-session` or `koa-session`, `idleTimeout` is their `rolling` option. The difference is that it carries its own duration instead of reinterpreting `maxAge`, so enabling it does not cost you the absolute limit.

Resealing is the expensive part of a session, so H3 does not do it on every request: it reseals only once more than half the window has been used, and updating the session counts as a reseal. An active user therefore never gets signed out, but the recorded last-seen time can trail the real one by up to half the window:
// Sign-out happens 15 to 30 minutes after the last request, never later.
Halve `idleTimeout` if you need the shorter end of that range to be your real limit.
> Only cookie sessions slide. A session sent through the `x-{name}-session` header cannot be resealed, so it expires `idleTimeout` after its seal was issued.

> Because the session lives in the cookie, a request that only reads the session writes it back when it slides the window. If such a request overlaps with one that writes the session, whichever response the browser applies last wins, so the write can be lost. Without `idleTimeout` a read-only request sets no cookie and cannot clobber a concurrent write.

> A request that slides the window pays for an extra seal and puts a `Set-Cookie` header on its response — shared caches and CDNs often refuse to store those. Requests that only read the session inside the throttle window set no cookie at all.
The session cookie is also applied to error responses, so a request that throws still slides the window and still persists a session created during it.

The PR deletes timezone-aware overrides (getHours/setHours, getMinutes/setMinutes, setSeconds, setMilliseconds etc.) that delegate to internal UTC state and sync, so TZDateMini will revert to native Date behavior and return/set wrong wall-clock values for its time zone.

Marked regions delete core Date API overrides (get*/set* for year/month/date/hours/minutes/seconds/ms) so any caller using TZDateMini.getMonth/setMinutes etc will get wrong timezone handling or missing method.

Marked hunk deletes TZDateMini Date overrides (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate/getDay/getHours/getMinutes and set*); fallback is native Date local-time behavior and loss of syncToInternal/syncFromInternal, breaking timezone-adjusted callers.

Deleted methods syncToInternal/syncFromInternal/fixDST handle timezone offset/DST correction; if any remaining code still calls them the class will crash or return wrong wall-time, and without them DST transitions will be off.
